prompt: Why did Caesar build a second line facing outward at Alesia?

options.text: To defend against a Gallic relief army
To give the town a new water supply
To provide an unguarded civilian exit
To replace the first line after abandoning the siege

explanation: The outward-facing line defended the Romans against forces coming to relieve Alesia. The inner line kept the siege in place. Caesar's army occupied the corridor between them.

feedbackByOptionId.gallia-03-a: One line contained Alesia; the other faced its rescuers. Caesar had arranged to besiege and be besieged at the same address.
feedbackByOptionId.gallia-03-b: The second line faced the relief army. Water engineering was already on the first line's rather long list of jobs.
feedbackByOptionId.gallia-03-c: The outward line blocked the relief army. An unguarded exit was not a feature of this siege.
feedbackByOptionId.gallia-03-d: The first line stayed: the second faced the relief army. Caesar doubled the fortifications rather than abandoning the siege.

sources.label: Caesar, Bellum Gallicum VII.74 — the second line, fourteen miles, facing outward
